original_question: Which G protein-coupled receptor is mutated in the rare genetic disorder characterized by abnormal ossification of the endocrine system and accelerated skeletal maturation?

final_qi.question: Which G protein-coupled receptor is mutated in the rare genetic disorder characterized by abnormal ossification of the endocrine system and accelerated skeletal maturation?
final_qi.long_answer: Jansen’s metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, a very rare disorder marked by abnormal (ectopic and premature) ossification and markedly accelerated skeletal maturation, is caused by activating mutations in the parathyroid hormone/parathyroid hormone-related peptide receptor 1 (PTH1R), a class B G protein-coupled receptor. Constitutive signaling of mutant PTH1R disrupts normal endochondral bone development, producing the characteristic skeletal abnormalities.

final_answer.long_answer: Blomstrand chondrodysplasia is a rare autosomal-recessive disorder marked by premature, extensive ossification of endocrine glands (e.g., pancreas, adrenal, thyroid) and markedly accelerated skeletal maturation. It is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the parathyroid hormone/parathyroid hormone-related peptide receptor type 1 (PTH1R), a class B G protein-coupled receptor that mediates PTH/PTHrP signaling essential for normal endochondral bone development.
